items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: You could go from an Elvis song number one, and number two might be Mitch Miller.

ctx.x: and I can do it. So you’re not just stuck with I can only play this style or that style. So I think that’s kind of what we had going for us. If you wanted to work, you had to be able to play whatever’s on the radio, and it could be any style.

Yes. And the radio, I remember recently looking at Billboard’s Top 10 from back in those years, and it was so varied. You could go from an Elvis song number one, and number two might be Mitch Miller. I mean, and the same playlist.

Right. And Sinatra with Basie. Yeah. All that Top 40 or whatever, it was very diversified. That changed a lot. And I think you mentioned in some of the pre-questions you gave me of things to think about, what to tell younger students who are interested in becoming musicians. And I want to skip to that because it goes right along with what we’re talking about is diversification of styles, learning more about not only how to play your instrument but, as much as I love jazz, there are other elements of music that…
